jobs.description:
Director of Technology- Process Development & Scale-Up

ElementUSA is seeking a Director of Technology – Process Development & Scale-Up to provide technical leadership across the development, scale-up, and commercialization of novel mineral and materials processing technologies. This role will lead and challenge multidisciplinary technical teams working across both hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical processes, ensuring laboratory and pilot development is focused not only on technical performance, but also on scalability, operability, economics, and commercial execution.

The Director will work closely with PhD scientists, metallurgists, chemists, process engineers, project managers, operations personnel, equipment suppliers, and external engineering partners to translate experimental results into maturing process flowsheets, design criteria, equipment requirements, and engineering packages.

A critical responsibility of this position will be establishing the technical-development management system that connects test campaigns, technical risks, pilot capabilities, process flowsheet maturity, engineering requirements, and scale-up decisions.

Technology & Process Development
Provide technical leadership across hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical process-development programs.
Lead, mentor, manage, and constructively challenge PhD scientists, metallurgists, chemists, and process-development personnel.
Review test campaigns to ensure clear objectives, hypotheses, success criteria, priorities, and actionable outcomes.
Challenge assumptions and results related to mass balances, recoveries, selectivity, reagent consumption, impurity behavior, energy requirements, process conditions, and scalability.
Drive maturation of integrated process flowsheets from laboratory concepts through pilot-scale demonstration and commercial readiness.
Identify critical technical unknowns and develop structured test programs to systematically retire technical and scale-up risks.
Ensure development work generates the data required for engineering design, economic evaluation, and commercial decision-making.

Technology Development Governance & Execution
Establish and maintain a practical management system for technology and process-development activities across laboratory, pilot, and scale-up programs.
Develop and manage KPIs, scorecards, trackers, and review cadences that provide clear visibility into technical progress, priorities, risks, decisions, and next steps.
Maintain an integrated view of active and planned test campaigns, including objectives, technical questions, success criteria, owners, schedules, results, conclusions, and follow-up actions.
Ensure testing is tied to specific flowsheet decisions, technical risks, scale-up requirements, engineering inputs, or economic assumptions rather than testing for testing's sake.
Develop and maintain a technical risk and unknowns register with defined test plans for retiring critical uncertainties.
Develop a pilot equipment and capability roadmap identifying what equipment is required, why it is needed, which test or scale-up objective it supports, timing, cost, and readiness.
Challenge proposed pilot equipment purchases to ensure capital is aligned with the process-development and commercialization roadmap.
Track technology maturity by major unit operation from concept to laboratory proof, pilot demonstration, engineering design basis, commissioning, and operations.
Establish technical readiness criteria and stage gates for advancing technologies into the next phase.
Lead recurring technology reviews focused on results, risks, decisions, priorities, and next experiments rather than activity reporting.
Provide the COO and executive leadership with a concise view of technical maturity, unresolved risks, upcoming decisions, resource requirements, and readiness for scale-up.

Scale-Up & Engineering Translation
Serve as a primary technical bridge between process development and engineering execution teams.
Translate laboratory and pilot results into process design criteria, mass and energy balances, process flow diagrams, equipment requirements, operating parameters, and other engineering inputs.
Work closely with project management and engineering teams to ensure technology packages are sufficiently mature before advancing into detailed engineering and capital execution.
Participate in equipment specification, vendor technical evaluations, pilot equipment selection, engineering reviews, and design decisions.
Clearly distinguish what has been demonstrated, what remains uncertain, and what additional testing is required before design assumptions are frozen.
Understand and support the progression from concept and FEL/design through procurement, construction, commissioning, startup, and steady-state operations.
Remain engaged through engineering, commissioning, and startup to ensure process-development intent is successfully translated into operating equipment.

Techno-Economic & Commercialization Support
Incorporate economic thinking throughout process development rather than treating economics as a downstream activity.
Evaluate process decisions considering recovery, selectivity, reagent consumption, energy demand, throughput, equipment requirements, waste generation, recycle streams, CAPEX, and OPEX implications.
Work with Engineering, Operations, Finance, and leadership to identify the major technical and economic drivers affecting commercial viability.
Help establish technical and economic stage gates for advancing technologies from laboratory development through pilot and commercial scale.
Identify development pathways that may be technically achievable but commercially impractical and recommend alternatives.

Pilot & Operations Support
Support commissioning, startup, troubleshooting, and optimization of pilot and demonstration equipment.
Ensure lessons learned during pilot operations are captured and incorporated into future process and engineering designs.
Partner with Operations to establish operating windows, critical process parameters, sampling requirements, process controls, and operating procedures.
Support root-cause analysis and technical troubleshooting as technologies transition from development into continuous operation.
Maintain a strong connection between laboratory development and real-world plant operability, maintainability, safety, reliability, and workforce requirements.

Leadership & Organization Development
Manage and develop a multidisciplinary technical organization that may include PhD scientists, metallurgists, chemists, process engineers, laboratory personnel, and technical specialists.
Establish clear priorities, accountability, development objectives, and technical ownership across the team.
Create a culture where technical assumptions are constructively challenged and decisions are driven by data.
Balance scientific exploration with schedule, cost, commercialization priorities, and company objectives.
Develop technical talent and organizational capability as the company progresses from early-stage process development into commercial operations.

Candidate Profile
Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Mineral Processing, Extractive Metallurgy, or a related discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
Significant industrial experience across both hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy, ideally involving mineral processing, extractive metallurgy, critical minerals, metals refining, recycling, or related process industries.
Demonstrated experience developing and scaling processes from laboratory through pilot and/or commercial operation.
Strong understanding of hydrometallurgical operations such as leaching, precipitation, filtration, solvent extraction, ion exchange, crystallization, and solid/liquid separation.
Strong understanding of pyrometallurgical operations such as reduction, roasting, calcination, furnaces, thermal processing, gas handling, and solids processing.
Demonstrated ability to lead, manage, mentor, and challenge highly technical scientists and PhD-level personnel.
Experience developing process flowsheets, mass balances, design criteria, process-engineering deliverables, and structured technical-development programs.
Working knowledge of capital project development and engineering execution, including stage-gate/FEL processes, project management, equipment specification, vendor engagement, engineering reviews, commissioning, and startup.
Strong understanding of the relationship between process performance and commercial economics.
Demonstrated people-management experience and ability to build high-performing technical teams.
Strong communication skills with the ability to translate highly technical information into clear recommendations for executive leadership, engineering, operations, and commercial stakeholders.

Join Us

If you’re excited by the idea of advancing sustainable mineral science and want your analytical work to make a measurable impact, we’d love to hear from you.

NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

NVIDIA’s advanced datacenter boards push forward chip packaging, PCB fabrication, SMT, assembly, and testing capabilities. Dedicated teams take responsibility for each technology: packaging manages the package, PCB and materials handle fabrication and stack-up, SMT and assembly oversee build processes, and test and SI focus on test capabilities. The challenge is to align these improvements across the stack—from chip to PCB, PCB to SMT, SMT to assembly, and assembly to test. Each domain’s innovation delivers maximum benefit when downstream consequences are considered early. The Senior Director, Board PDE oversees integration methods that make this possible—coordinating handoffs, engineering cross-domain effects before changes, and optimizing the entire chain.

What You'll Be Doing

Design, implement, and institutionalize the integration readiness process for all next-generation datacenter board products — owning manufacturing and test readiness end to end so build starts land on schedule and at target yield.
Guide the functional teams in developing cross-boundary techniques before silicon and stackup freeze occurs. Focus on warpage-tolerant DFM and reflow for next-gen BGA pitch. Manage impedance and CTE control for high-speed stackups. Lock pad-map and fab methods at an early stage.
Build, lead, and develop a global Board PDE organization across three technical pillars — PCB & Fab, SMT/PCBA, and High-Speed Connector & Signal Integrity.
Set up integration oversight throughout the chip-to-board stack. Define entry and exit requirements at each domain boundary. Lead the gates to confirm one qualified domain is ready to pass to the next.
Collaborate with Operations Test Engineering and Signal Integrity to establish test coverage and manufacturing test flow requirements, applying that thoroughness to the tester and diagnostic boards.
Take charge of reliability and yield performance throughout the stack. Investigate excursions to identify root causes. Address DFx and alternate-component gaps with the factory planning and design teams.
Support manufacturing partners (CM/ODM/OSAT, substrate, and PCB fab) in producing world-class datacenter products. Serve as the senior chip-to-board representative across NVIDIA's Operations, Engineering, and Executive teams.

What We Need To See

Overview:

At Capital One, we are creating trustworthy and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good. For years, Capital One has been leading the industry in using machine learning to create real-time, intelligent, automated customer experiences. From informing customers about unusual charges to answering their questions in real time, our applications of AI & ML are bringing humanity and simplicity to banking. We are committed to building world-class applied science and engineering teams and continue our industry leading capabilities with breakthrough product experiences and scalable, high-performance AI infrastructure. At Capital One, you will help bring the transformative power of emerging AI capabilities to reimagine how we serve our customers and businesses who have come to love the products and services we build.

Team Description:

The AI Foundations team is at the center of bringing our vision for AI at Capital One to life. Our work touches every aspect of the research life cycle, from partnering with Academia to building production systems. We work with product, technology and business leaders to apply the state of the art in AI to our business.

This is a people manager role that will lead teams to drive strategic direction through collaboration with Applied Science, Engineering and Product leaders across Capital One. As a well-respected people leader, you will guide and mentor a team of applied scientists. You will be expected to be an external leader representing Capital One in the research community, collaborating with prominent faculty members in the relevant AI research community.

In this role, you will:

Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, machine learning engineers and product managers to deliver AI-powered products that change how customers interact with their money.
Leverage a broad stack of technologies — Pytorch, AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, Lightning, VectorDBs, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual data.
Build AI foundation models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementation.
Engage in high impact applied research to take the latest AI developments and push them into the next generation of customer experiences.
Flex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals.

The Ideal Candidate:

You love the process of analyzing and creating, but also share our passion to do the right thing. You know at the end of the day it’s about making the right decision for our customers.
Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them.
Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea.
A leader. You challenge conventional thinking and work with stakeholders to identify and improve the status quo. You’re passionate about talent development for your own team and beyond.
Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing AI foundation models and solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms.
Has a deep understanding of the foundations of AI methodologies.
Experience building large deep learning models, whether on language, images, events, or graphs, as well as expertise in one or more of the following: training optimization, self-supervised learning, robustness, explainability, RLHF.

Experience in delivering libraries, platform level code or solution level code to existing products.
A professional with a track record of coming up with new ideas or improving upon existing ideas in machine learning, demonstrated by accomplishments such as first author publications or projects.
Possess the ability to own and pursue a research agenda, including choosing impactful research problems and autonomously carrying out long-running projects.

Partner with a cross-functional team of scientists, machine learning engineers, software engineers, and product managers to deliver AI-powered platforms and solutions that change how customers interact with their money.
Build AI foundation models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementation.
Engage in high impact applied research to take the latest AI developments and push them into the next generation of customer experiences.
Leverage a broad stack of technologies — Pytorch, AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, Lightning, VectorDBs, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual data.
Flex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals.

PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, AI, Mathematics, or related fields plus 6 years of experience in Applied Research or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, AI, Mathematics, or related fields plus 8 years of experience in Applied Research
At least 5 years of people leadership experience

PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Electrical Engineering or related fields
LLM
PhD focus on NLP or Masters with 10 years of industrial NLP research experience
Core contributor to team that has trained a large language model from scratch (10B + parameters, 500B+ tokens)
Numerous publications at ACL, NAACL and EMNLP, Neurips, ICML or ICLR on topics related to the pre-training of large language models (e.g. technical reports of pre-trained LLMs, SSL techniques, model pre-training optimization)

Demonstrated ability to guide the technical direction of a large-scale model training team
Experience working with 500+ node clusters of GPUs Has worked on LLM scaled to 70B parameters and 1T+ tokens
Experience with common training optimization frameworks (deep speed, nemo)

Behavioral Models

Member of technical leadership for model deployment for a very large user behavior model

Proposed new methods for inference or representation learning on graphs or sequences
Worked datasets with 100m+ users

Experience deploying a fine-tuned large language model

Leading contributions to one or more large open source corpus (1 Trillion + tokens)
Core contributor to open source libraries for data quality, dataset curation, or labeling

Pay Range

Churchill Downs Racetrack (“CDRT”), the world’s most legendary racetrack, has been the home of The Kentucky Derby, the longest continually held annual sporting event in the United States, since 1875. The Director, Broadcast Engineering is responsible for leading all broadcast engineering operations supporting Churchill Downs Racetrack's live racing, television productions, simulcast operations, and special events. This hands-on leadership role oversees the installation, operation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of broadcast, audio, video, and broadcast IT systems that ensure reliable, high-quality production and venue operations.

Broadcast Engineering & Technical Operations

Install, configure, maintain, and support broadcast equipment, videoboard operations, venue audio systems, and broadcast IT infrastructure.
Configure and support Evertz routers, RTS intercom systems, KVM systems, QSC audio systems, Dante audio networks, QAM headend systems, and fiber optic infrastructure.

Coordinate frequency management and signal distribution for major live events.

Lead and manage the broadcast engineering team while overseeing multiple technical projects and live event operations.

Provide technical leadership and make real-time operational decisions in a high-pressure live production environment.

Develop and maintain a multi-year lifecycle and technology roadmap for broadcast, audio, video, network, and supporting software infrastructure.
Proactively identify aging, unsupported, or end-of-life technologies and devices and participate in annual capital planning and budgeting to ensure critical systems are refreshed, upgraded, or replaced before they create operational, security, or reliability risks.

Broadcast Partner Support

Serve as the primary engineering liaison with broadcast partners regarding technical setup and venue requirements.
Collaborate with internal teams and external vendors to support successful broadcast operations and live event execution.
Perform other duties as assigned.

REGULATORY

Ability to obtain and maintain a Kentucky racing license and successfully complete all applicable background check requirements.

Required Skills And Abilities

Advanced knowledge of broadcast engineering systems and live production operations.
Strong leadership, project management, process, and engineering team development skills.
Expertise supporting broadcast control room operations and production workflows.
Proficiency with QSC audio systems, Dante audio networking, Evertz routing systems, RTS intercom systems, and KVM infrastructure.
Strong understanding of broadcast IT networks, signal distribution, fiber optic systems, and RF frequency coordination.
Excellent troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and perform effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.
Strong communication skills with demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across Broadcast Engineering, Information Technology, Information Security, Operations, and external partners, including shared ownership of troubleshooting and issue resolution.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and standard engineering documentation software.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree required; 12+ years of relevant broadcast engineering experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
10+ years of engineering management experience supporting broadcast or live production environments.
Demonstrated experience supporting live television broadcasts, studio productions, and major live events.
Experience in a sports venue required; horse racing experience preferred.
Experience with QSC audio systems, Dante networking, broadcast IT systems, fiber optic infrastructure, and venue broadcast operations.
QSC, Dante, Society of Broadcast Engineers (SBE), and Fiber Optic certifications preferred.
Experience with AutoCAD and Bluebeam Revu preferred.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

Ability to lift, move, and install broadcast equipment weighing up to 70 pounds.
Ability to work on ladders, rooftops, elevated platforms, and in confined spaces.
Regular standing, walking, climbing, bending, kneeling, and moving throughout the facility to support engineering operations.
Ability to work evenings, weekends, holidays, rotating schedules, and extended hours as required to support racing events and live broadcasts.
Ability to perform effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure live production environment.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

Churchill Downs Incorporated is an inclusive and fun place to work. We celebrate unique approaches and points of view. We believe diversity is a mindset that drives excellence. We’re always learning, evolving and growing. We innovate through mutual respect of ideas and collaboration. jobs.description:
Aderant is a global industry leading software company providing comprehensive business management solutions for law firms and other professional services organizations with a mission to help them run a better business. We are motivated by a collective desire to drive the legal industry to the forefront of innovation. With over 2,500 clients around the world, including 95 of the top AmLaw 100 firms, we are changing the outside perception of the legal sphere; where there was once resistance to modernization, we are creating a culture that embraces new ideas and technology.

At Aderant, the “A” is more than just a letter. It is a representation of how we fulfill our foundational purpose, serving our clients. It embodies our core values and reminds us that to achieve success, every day must start with the “A”. We bring the “A” to life by fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and personal growth. We encourage our diverse teams to bring their whole selves to work – ideas, experience, and passion – to drive our mission forward.

Our people are our strength.

Role Overview

Aderant is seeking a Head of Infrastructure to serve as a key member of the technology leadership team, reporting directly to the Chief Technology Officer (CTO).

This role is responsible for the end-to-end strategy, delivery, and operation of Aderant’s global infrastructure platforms across AWS and Microsoft Azure, supporting both product engineering and customer-facing SaaS environments.

The Head of Infrastructure will lead multiple global teams, including Cloud Operations (Sierra and platform operations) and DevOps, bringing together currently distributed capabilities into a unified, scalable operating model.

A primary focus of this role will be the evolution and reliability of Aderant’s Sierra cloud environments, which are predominantly single-tenant deployments, alongside enabling consistent infrastructure, deployment, and operational practices across all products.

This leader will establish clear ownership across infrastructure, platform services, DevOps, and cloud operations—driving standardization, reliability, and efficiency while enabling engineering teams to deliver at scale.

Infrastructure Strategy & Organizational Leadership

Build and scale high-performing global teams, including senior leaders across Cloud Operations and DevOps.

Standardize monitoring, alerting, and incident management across all platforms.
Lead global incident response, on-call structures, and post-incident review processes.

Enable engineering teams through self-service infrastructure, automation, and standardized tooling.

Establish reusable platform services and shared infrastructure capabilities across products.

Support both single-tenant and multi-tenant SaaS models through scalable infrastructure design.

Oversee capacity planning, performance optimization, and regional infrastructure strategy.
Ensure effective workload placement and resource utilization across environments.

Director of Technology- Process Development & Scale-Up

ElementUSA is seeking a Director of Technology – Process Development & Scale-Up to provide technical leadership across the development, scale-up, and commercialization of novel mineral and materials processing technologies. This role will lead and challenge multidisciplinary technical teams working across both hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical processes, ensuring laboratory and pilot development is focused not only on technical performance, but also on scalability, operability, economics, and commercial execution.

The Director will work closely with PhD scientists, metallurgists, chemists, process engineers, project managers, operations personnel, equipment suppliers, and external engineering partners to translate experimental results into maturing process flowsheets, design criteria, equipment requirements, and engineering packages.

A critical responsibility of this position will be establishing the technical-development management system that connects test campaigns, technical risks, pilot capabilities, process flowsheet maturity, engineering requirements, and scale-up decisions.

Technology & Process Development
Provide technical leadership across hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical process-development programs.
Lead, mentor, manage, and constructively challenge PhD scientists, metallurgists, chemists, and process-development personnel.
Review test campaigns to ensure clear objectives, hypotheses, success criteria, priorities, and actionable outcomes.
Challenge assumptions and results related to mass balances, recoveries, selectivity, reagent consumption, impurity behavior, energy requirements, process conditions, and scalability.
Drive maturation of integrated process flowsheets from laboratory concepts through pilot-scale demonstration and commercial readiness.
Identify critical technical unknowns and develop structured test programs to systematically retire technical and scale-up risks.
Ensure development work generates the data required for engineering design, economic evaluation, and commercial decision-making.

Technology Development Governance & Execution
Establish and maintain a practical management system for technology and process-development activities across laboratory, pilot, and scale-up programs.
Develop and manage KPIs, scorecards, trackers, and review cadences that provide clear visibility into technical progress, priorities, risks, decisions, and next steps.
Maintain an integrated view of active and planned test campaigns, including objectives, technical questions, success criteria, owners, schedules, results, conclusions, and follow-up actions.
Ensure testing is tied to specific flowsheet decisions, technical risks, scale-up requirements, engineering inputs, or economic assumptions rather than testing for testing's sake.
Develop and maintain a technical risk and unknowns register with defined test plans for retiring critical uncertainties.
Develop a pilot equipment and capability roadmap identifying what equipment is required, why it is needed, which test or scale-up objective it supports, timing, cost, and readiness.
Challenge proposed pilot equipment purchases to ensure capital is aligned with the process-development and commercialization roadmap.
Track technology maturity by major unit operation from concept to laboratory proof, pilot demonstration, engineering design basis, commissioning, and operations.
Establish technical readiness criteria and stage gates for advancing technologies into the next phase.
Lead recurring technology reviews focused on results, risks, decisions, priorities, and next experiments rather than activity reporting.
Provide the COO and executive leadership with a concise view of technical maturity, unresolved risks, upcoming decisions, resource requirements, and readiness for scale-up.

Scale-Up & Engineering Translation
Serve as a primary technical bridge between process development and engineering execution teams.
Translate laboratory and pilot results into process design criteria, mass and energy balances, process flow diagrams, equipment requirements, operating parameters, and other engineering inputs.
Work closely with project management and engineering teams to ensure technology packages are sufficiently mature before advancing into detailed engineering and capital execution.
Participate in equipment specification, vendor technical evaluations, pilot equipment selection, engineering reviews, and design decisions.
Clearly distinguish what has been demonstrated, what remains uncertain, and what additional testing is required before design assumptions are frozen.
Understand and support the progression from concept and FEL/design through procurement, construction, commissioning, startup, and steady-state operations.
Remain engaged through engineering, commissioning, and startup to ensure process-development intent is successfully translated into operating equipment.

Techno-Economic & Commercialization Support
Incorporate economic thinking throughout process development rather than treating economics as a downstream activity.
Evaluate process decisions considering recovery, selectivity, reagent consumption, energy demand, throughput, equipment requirements, waste generation, recycle streams, CAPEX, and OPEX implications.
Work with Engineering, Operations, Finance, and leadership to identify the major technical and economic drivers affecting commercial viability.
Help establish technical and economic stage gates for advancing technologies from laboratory development through pilot and commercial scale.
Identify development pathways that may be technically achievable but commercially impractical and recommend alternatives.

Pilot & Operations Support
Support commissioning, startup, troubleshooting, and optimization of pilot and demonstration equipment.
Ensure lessons learned during pilot operations are captured and incorporated into future process and engineering designs.
Partner with Operations to establish operating windows, critical process parameters, sampling requirements, process controls, and operating procedures.
Support root-cause analysis and technical troubleshooting as technologies transition from development into continuous operation.
Maintain a strong connection between laboratory development and real-world plant operability, maintainability, safety, reliability, and workforce requirements.

Leadership & Organization Development
Manage and develop a multidisciplinary technical organization that may include PhD scientists, metallurgists, chemists, process engineers, laboratory personnel, and technical specialists.
Establish clear priorities, accountability, development objectives, and technical ownership across the team.
Create a culture where technical assumptions are constructively challenged and decisions are driven by data.
Balance scientific exploration with schedule, cost, commercialization priorities, and company objectives.
Develop technical talent and organizational capability as the company progresses from early-stage process development into commercial operations.

Candidate Profile
Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Mineral Processing, Extractive Metallurgy, or a related discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
Significant industrial experience across both hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy, ideally involving mineral processing, extractive metallurgy, critical minerals, metals refining, recycling, or related process industries.

Strong understanding of hydrometallurgical operations such as leaching, precipitation, filtration, solvent extraction, ion exchange, crystallization, and solid/liquid separation.

Experience developing process flowsheets, mass balances, design criteria, process-engineering deliverables, and structured technical-development programs.

Strong communication skills with the ability to translate highly technical information into clear recommendations for executive leadership, engineering, operations, and commercial stakeholders.
